methods.controls: Eight pairs of two-second stereo recordings. A continuous bed in both channels and a filtered noise in one. Onset and ongoing arms have identical PCM in both channels from the start of the 220 ms mark to the end. In the onset arm a different frequency band precedes the mark with a 4 ms crossfade at its left edge. The ongoing arm continues the target band. Butterworth order four, 24 kHz, hashed media and marked samples below.
methods.natural: Twelve separate Perception Test films outside the 56 prior audiovisual agreement films. Events with a specific label and duration of 2.1–9 s, without an immediately preceding overlapping annotation of that class. Deterministic hash ordering with salt reel-auditory-boundary-v1/, initially one example per distinct class. Two original two-second excerpts of each film: the mark meets the annotated event start or lies at least 1.25 s inside that event. Sound only. These are agreements with published event boundaries, which can span pauses. No new listeners heard the cuts.
methods.protocol: One fresh session per clip and version. Both see the same anonymous PCM through Reel, the same two-second conventional channel spectrogram, film clock, peak/pitch/change readings and question. Both can replay. The marked condition also supplies a 25 ms spectrogram with a 220 ms bracket. No answers or filenames, no visual scene, same amount of original audio. Answers new, ongoing or unclear. An unclear answer scores zero. Stimuli, question wording, protocol and case order frozen before responses. The collected prototype and shipped code return identical marked sample ranges and PNG hashes on all 40 clips. The prototype and release differ in their tool descriptions and in handling marks at rounded boundaries between playback turns. Attribution includes the improved diagram, bracket and tool instructions together.
methods.bootstrap: Resample entire stimulus pairs (including both answers in both versions), 10000 draws, seed 20261123. Conditional on the chosen films and single responses.

encoder_pilot.method: Existing CLAP at recorded gain. Rank the two stored descriptions by their cosine averaged across active channels. Compare the exact excerpt padded once with zeros, repeated padding, one additional second of the original on each available side, the same context with the event samples zeroed, and the difference between the containing and zeroed clip cosines. This exploratory comparison is outside the product path. A counterfactual edit can itself affect the score.
